about: Upstreams the NPU route depends on but does not vendor, each pinned to the commit that was last reviewed, plus the d3 weight repos that exist. tools/census_watch.py alerts when a pinned commit moves or a d3 repo appears that is not listed here, so both are looked at before they reach a release. To clear an alert, read the change, then update the commit and `reviewed` (or add the repo to `d3_sources.known`) in this file - that edit is the record of the review.

ROCm/FLM_Q4NX_Converter.why: The official gguf Q4_0/Q4_1 -> Q4NX converter with per-architecture configs (configs/*.json, 18 of them: gemma3, gemma4, gpt-oss, lfm2, llama, nanbeige, phi4, qwen2, qwen2vl, qwen3, qwen3.5_{0.8b,2b,4b,9b,a3b,omni}, qwen3vl). docs/npu.md's repack path runs it (scripts/repack_gguf.py, ONEBIT_Q4NX_CONVERTER) and fails its declared-scale guard when the converter or config drops a critical scale. A per-arch config here is what makes a family packable on our side at all.  Reviewed 2026-11-08 (d1d5232 -> 93b8398, 2 commits, "Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.5-MoE / Omni converters on stock llama.cpp GGUFs"): three changes touch the family this route serves. (a) full-attention layers are now detected from `attn_q.weight` instead of "every Nth layer", because the d3 layouts are irregular -- the commit names full attention at 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 for d3:edge, which is the same irregularity our own converter takes from `layer_types`; (b) an MTP block (nextn_predict_layers > 0, counted in block_count) no longer leaks out as a bogus extra decoder layer; (c) the Qwen35 value-head reorder is decided from the v/qk head ratio instead of feed_forward_length <= 6144, and a ratio > 2 raises. Stock Qwen3.5 0.8B/2B/4B (Q4_K, Q4_1) are tested 124/124 in that PR, and the output is byte-identical for GGUFs without an MTP block, so the repack path's declared-scale guard is unaffected; the entry point and configs/ layout that scripts/repack_gguf.py invokes are unchanged.

vllm-project/semantic-router.why: The Decision 3.0 (d3) source: the router calls d3 for routing, guardrails and tool selection, and FastFlowLM v1.0.11 serves those weights through /v1/systemone with the same HTTP API as the upstream d3 server. Engine #653 is our side of that; a change here is what a new d3 pack would follow.  Reviewed 2026-11-08 (632f087 -> b7adcfa, 152 commits, 300 files): **the d3 contract is unchanged** -- `d3_format.py`, `d3_server.py` and `d3_runtime.py` are not in the delta at all, and the only System One files touched are dashboard frontend pages (`SystemOnePlaygroundPage.tsx`, `systemOneTargets.ts`). What moved is router-side: `config/fragments/signal/decision/vela{2,3}-labels-spans.yaml` (their own newer decision models), a `config/recipes/decision-balance/` recipe, and a `canonical_decision_model` CRD. So what this route must speak is unchanged, and the vela2/vela3 names are upstream's packs, not ours.  Reviewed 2026-11-09 (b7adcfa -> a921924, 9 commits, engine #1667): the d3 contract is unchanged again -- no d3_* file is in the delta. The one System One file is the router's client, pkg/systemone/backend.go (#5144): a backend marked trusted_gateway is now refused before dispatch (errTrustedGatewayUnsupported), because System One dispatch does not carry the request's gateway credential. The wire protocol string stays vllm-sr/systemone@1, and FastFlowLM's /v1/systemone is not a trusted gateway, so nothing this route speaks or serves moves. The rest is router-side (header_mutation append, the lifecycle client's 5xx retry, contrastive jailbreak embedding validation, adaptive thinking on Responses backends, a repeated [DONE] in protocolcodec) plus a Claude Code plugin and maintainer docs.

d3_sources.about: HF repos under the vllm-sr org whose name starts with `d3` are the decision-model weights FastFlowLM packs as FastFlowLM/D3-*-NPU2 (base_model tags point here). A new one is a new pack on the way. Reviewed 2026-11-08: `d3-ultra-INT4` (17.6 GB), `d3-ultra-FP8` (31.9 GB) and `d3-ultra-NVFP4` (51.6 GB) are the quantization variants of `d3-ultra`, each with its own `config.json` and `decision_config.json` (i.e. real d3 packs, not derivative drops), so they are listed here rather than treated as new families.
